items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: So during that time I was talking to Mulgrew that I didn’t really understand modes.

ctx.x: got at Birdland. So somebody called and said, “You ain’t got no two weeks.” So I got up and my wife said, “Oh by the way call Betty Carter, she’s got two weeks for you at Birdland.” I was just, it was maybe five years, I don’t know. So she said also, “Do you know somebody named Prophet?” Well Prophet, his name was Richard Jennings, he was a well talented artist, he could draw pictures and paintings with birds, and Miles loved him and everybody knew him. And he knew I could comp. And Joe Griffin knew I could comp.…

during that time he had been known to maybe do that, “I changed my mind.” Because what he did, like on the “Seven Steps to Heaven” date, that was conceived when I was in the band on that tour. And we had a great time. Jimmy Cobb will tell you about it, Roy talks about it in the book. There was me, so he asked me, “Do you know a good alto player?” I said, “Yeah, Frank Strozier.” He said, “What’s Frank doin’?” Because he knew us from Chicago. So I told Frank to go by but Frank was reluctant. So his wife says, “No…
